title: Cucumber and Radish Salad
description: Love the flavors of fresh veggies? Then give this cucumber and radish salad a taste! Paired with fresh herbs and an easy salad dressing, it’s a great appetizer or side salad for any meal needing a bit more color.
steps: In a large bowl, combine the thinly sliced cucumbers, radishes, red onion, chopped fresh dill, and fresh parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk together the white wine vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the cucumber, radish, and herb mixture.
Toss the salad gently to ensure even coating.
Allow the salad to marinate in the refrigerator for at least 15 minutes to enhance the flavors.

title: Budget-Friendly Greek Salad and Grilled Shrimp Pitas
description: Serve this dish with a cup of cold gazpacho soup or with sautéed zucchini seasoned with lemon juice and oregano.
ingredients: 1/2 large, or 1 small cucumber(s) (peeled and sliced)
steps: Prepare an indoor or outdoor grill.
In a large bowl, toss together lettuce, onion, cucumber, feta cheese, olive oil, red wine vinegar, and oregano.
Fill each pita pocket half with 1/4 of lettuce mixture. Set aside.
Season shrimp with salt (optional), ground black pepper and cayenne pepper. Spray shrimp with cooking spray.
Grill shrimp for 3-4 minutes on each side. Remove from grill and add 3 shrimp to each pita.

title: Garden Harvest Soup
description: Adjust the veggies in this soup based on what you have in your refrigerator. Get creative with the veggie combination that you use!
ingredients: 2 cup vegetables (uncooked, chopped, such as any combination of bell peppers, carrots, green beans, yellow summer squash, or zucchini)
2 cup low sodium chicken broth (low-sodium vegetable broth or fat-free, low-sodium)
1 cup fresh spinach leaves (loosely packed, coarsely chopped)
steps: In a medium saucepan, heat the oil over medium heat, swirling to coat the bottom. Cook the 2 cups chopped vegetables, onion, and seasoning blend for 8 to 10 minutes, or until tender-crisp, stirring occasionally. (If the vegetables get dry or start to scorch, add a little water to the saucepan.)

Stir in the broth. Increase the heat to medium high and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes so the flavors blend, stirring occasionally. Stir in the spinach. Sprinkle each serving with Parmesan cheese.

Tips: Chop firmer vegetables, such as carrots, into smaller pieces than more tender vegetables, such as zucchini, so all the vegetables will cook at about the same rate. If you want this dish to be vegetarian, be sure to use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth.

title: Whole Wheat Fresh Gingerbread
description: This fresh gingerbread loaf is a wholesome twist on a classic favorite, offering the warm, spicy notes of ginger and molasses, but with the goodness of whole wheat flour. It's a delightful addition to your holiday spread that the whole family is sure to enjoy! This diabetes-friendly is a great option to bring to a holiday cookie swap or to serve at your holiday meal to celebrate the season.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, brown sugar substitute, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves.
In another bowl, combine the applesauce, maple syrup, vegetable oil, freshly grated ginger, eggs, and vanilla extract. Mix until well combined.
Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, stirring until just combined. Do not overmix.
Slowly pour in the hot water while gently stirring the batter. The batter will be thin.
Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 45–50 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the bread comes out clean.
Once baked, remove the gingerbread from the oven and allow it to cool in the pan for about 10 minutes. Then, carefully remove it from the pan and transfer it to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Cold Cucumber Soup and Grilled Shrimp Open-Face Sandwich
description: Cool as a cucumber, this refreshing soup pairs perfectly with a grilled shrimp and spicy avocado aioli open-face sandwich. If the spice is too much, you can skip the hot sauce or just use a dash.
ingredients: 2 med cucumber(s) (cut in thirds and in half lengthwise)
4 tbsp lemon juice (from 2 med lemons, divided)
steps: To make the soup, place half of the cucumbers in a food processor fit with the chopping blade. Process until it is cut into small pieces. Add the remaining cucumber sections and process until they are cut into small pieces.
Add the yogurt, lemon juice, lemon zest, and dill and process until liquified and all cucumber pieces are puréed.

Spray a grill pan or outdoor grill with cooking spray and heat to medium. Toss the shrimp with olive oil and black pepper. Place on the preheated grill and cook for 1 minute. Flip the shrimp and cook for an additional minute. Shrimp cooks quickly, so be careful not to overcook it. Remove it from the grill to a plate.
In a small bowl, mash the avocado and add the mayonnaise, lemon juice, and hot sauce, and mix until light green in color and the avocado is incorporated and smooth.
Spread 1 Tbsp of the avocado aioli over each slice of toast. Top with ¼ cup of arugula and 3 shrimp. Serve with 1 ¼ cup of the soup on the side.

title: Sheet Pan Tofu Fajitas
description: Sheet pan dinners are a quick and easy way to enjoy a nutritious meal without a lot of clean up. This diabetes-friendly tofu fajitas meal is one the whole family will love and uses plant-based protein to keep you full and satisfied.
ingredients: 16 oz extra firm tofu (pressed and cubed)
4 whole low carb whole wheat burrito wraps
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Press the tofu to remove excess water, then cut it into cubes.
In a large bowl, combine tofu cubes, sliced bell peppers, and sliced red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, taco seasoning, ground cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, and black pepper to create the marinade.
Pour the marinade over the tofu and vegetables. Toss until everything is evenly coated. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Spread the marinated tofu and vegetables evenly on the sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 25 minutes or until the tofu is golden and the vegetables are tender, stirring halfway through.
Divide the fajita filling among the wraps.
Serve the sheet pan tofu fajitas and garnish with chopped cilantro and lime wedges.

title: Salad Bar Gazpacho Salad
description: This tasty salad uses a light tomato-based dressing and is packed with greens and other nutrient-rich veggies. Buy as many of these vegetables as you can precut from your grocer’s salad bar to save on prep time.
ingredients: 2 cup chickpeas, red kidney beans, or black beans (from salad bar or canned, drained and rinsed)
steps: Combine the beans, tomato, corn, cucumber, red onion, and cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk together the tomato juice, lime juice, olive oil, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Pour over the salad and mix gently. Serve over the mixed greens.

title: Sweet Potato Salad
description: Who says you can only use white potatoes for a potato salad? This dish will be a welcomed surprise at your next summer picnic.
steps: Peel sweet potatoes and cube. Place sweet potatoes in a large pot. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Boil until tender about 5-7 minutes. Drain potatoes and rinse with cold water; let cool.
While potatoes are cooking, cook bacon until crisp, then chop or crumble into small pieces.
In a small bowl, whisk together, olive oil, apple cider vinegar, pepper and garlic powder.
Place sweet potatoes in serving bowl and add celery, green onions and turkey bacon. Pour dressing over salad and toss until potatoes are coated. Serve cold.

title: Mango Mango Salad with Chicken
description: Traditional chicken salad is made a little more lively with the addition of mango! Find this recipe and more in The New Soul Food Cookbook for People with Diabetes.
ingredients: 1 med green bell pepper (seeded and chopped)
steps: Combine the mayonnaise and green onions in a small bowl, cover, and chill. Combine the chicken, mango, and bell pepper in a large bowl.
Combine the vinegar, lemon juice, and sugar in a container with a tight lid. Shake well. Add lemon mixture to the mayonnaise and green onion mixture and stir well.
Pour the dressing over the chicken and mango, toss well, and chill for 30 minutes. To serve, spoon onto a plate lined with lettuce leaves.

title: Crispy Potato Taco Bowl
description: This taco bowl features a hearty base of roasted white potatoes and fluffy cauliflower rice topped with savory ground beef, mushrooms, and red bell peppers. Fresh lime juice and cilantro brighten every bite, while creamy avocado adds richness and balance. It’s a satisfying, veggie-packed, high-fiber twist on classic taco flavors that’s easy enough for weeknights and perfect for build-your-own bowls.
ingredients: 12 oz white potatoes (about 2 medium, diced into 1/2-inch cubes)
1 cup red bell pepper (about 1 medium pepper, diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Toss diced potatoes with 1 1/2 tsp olive oil, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/8 tsp black pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 20–25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until tender and lightly browned.

In the same skillet, heat the remaining 1 1/2 tsp olive oil over medium heat. Add ground beef, chopped mushrooms, and diced red bell pepper. Cook for 8–10 minutes, breaking apart the beef, until meat is fully cooked and vegetables are tender.

Stir in chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Add the tomato sauce and water and bring to a simmer. Bring to a boil then reduce heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the liquid is reduced. Remove from heat.

While the beef mixture is simmering, heat cauliflower rice in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally until heated through. Add the cilantro and lime juice and mix together. Keep warm until ready to serve.
Divide the cauliflower rice evenly among four bowls. Top each bowl evenly with roasted potatoes, beef-mushroom-pepper mixture, two tomatoes, and 1/4 of a sliced avocado.

title: Plato de frutas arcoíris apto para niños
description: ¡Una receta rápida, fácil y colorida que cualquiera puede hacer! Pruébalo como desayuno, merienda o incluso postre.
ingredients: 8 oz yogur griego de vainilla (100 calorías)
1 piña fresca (pelado, sin corazón y en cubos (aproximadamente 4 tazas))
steps: Mezcla el yogur y las semillas de chía. Refrigere durante la noche. Mezcle 1/8 de cucharadita. canela.
En un plato muy grande, coloque las fresas en la fila superior formando la parte superior de un patrón de arcoíris.
Coloque los cubos de melón como segunda fila debajo de las fresas. Continúa este proceso con la piña pasando por las moras haciendo el patrón del arcoíris.

title: Korean BBQ-Inspired Baked Salmon
description: The Korean BBQ-inspired sauce on this salmon has that ideal balance of sweet, salty, tangy, and spicy. The sweetness comes naturally from fruit, not added sugars. You could also use this sauce on chicken: bake boneless, skinless chicken thighs without the sauce for 15 minutes, then brush on the sauce and bake for another 15 minutes, or until cooked through.
ingredients: 4 (6-oz) fillets center-cut sockeye salmon with skin
1 tbsp reduced-sodium tamari or soy sauce
steps: Preheat the oven to 400° F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the salmon, skin side down, on the baking sheet.

In a small bowl, stir together the ketchup, jam, tamari, vinegar, and hot pepper sauce. Lightly spread the mixture onto the top of each fillet using the back of the spoon. Sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Bake until the salmon is flaky and cooked through (with an internal temperature of at least 145°F), about 16 minutes. Serve.

title: Shrimp Sauté with Spinach, Grape Tomatoes, and Roasted Red Potatoes
description: This quick and delicious shrimp dish follows the Low Carb and Low Fat Eating Pattern, meaning it’s a good choice for people who are mindful of their blood pressure. Succulent shrimp are sautéed with fresh spinach, sweet grape tomatoes, and crispy roasted red potatoes, creating a harmonious blend of flavors and textures. It's a hearty and flavorful dish that's perfect for a weeknight dinner.
serving_size: 1 cup shrimp and veggies, ½ cup potatoes
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Halve or quarter the baby red potatoes, depending on their size. Toss them with 2 tsp olive oil, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast in the oven for 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden and tender.

Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add the remaining olive oil and grape tomatoes to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3–4 minutes, or until the tomatoes soften and release some of their juices
Add the garlic, shrimp, and crushed red pepper to the skillet. Sauté the shrimp for 1–2 minutes per side, or until opaque and cooked through.
Add the spinach to the skillet in handfuls, stirring after each addition to allow it to wilt.
Reduce the heat to low and sprinkle half the grated Parmesan cheese over the skillet contents. Stir to combine, allowing the cheese to melt slightly.
Divide the shrimp, sautéed veggies, and spinach between plates. Garnish with the reserved Parmesan cheese and basil ribbons. Serve alongside the roasted red potatoes.

title: Broccoli Onion Latkes
description: The low carb latkes use broccoli instead of the traditional potatoes. They are also lower in potassium, making them a great alternative for those following a low potassium diet for kidney health.
ingredients: 3 cup fresh or frozen chopped broccoli florets
steps: Boil the diced broccoli in a small amount of water for 5 minutes, then drain thoroughly.
Break eggs into a medium bowl and beat. Add the flour and mix well. Add the broccoli and onion and stir into the flour/egg mixture until well mixed.

Heat olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Drop the mixture by spoonfuls into the hot oil, making 4 equal portions. Flatten with a spatula, and cook until golden brown on both sides (about 3-4 minutes per side).
Remove the latkes from the pan and drain on a paper towel to soak up extra oil. Serve hot.

title: Besan Chilla
description: Made with chickpea flour and colorful vegetables, besan chilla is a popular savory pancake enjoyed in many Indian households. Its lightly nutty flavor, crisp edges, and tender center make it a tasty snack or light meal, while the chickpea flour provides protein and fiber.
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the besan, water, and spices until smooth.
Stir in the vegetables. Cover and set aside for 5-10 minutes. Mix well again.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat and lightly coat with cooking spray.
Pour the batter into the skillet, gently spread the batter evenly, and round off the shape to create a thin, 6-inch pancake.
Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until lightly browned and cooked through.
Serve warm with 1 Tbsp plain Greek yogurt on the side for dipping.

title: Nutritional Yeast
description: Nutrition information for 4 tbsp of nutritional yeast.

title: Creamy Mashed Cauliflower
description: Creamy Mashed Cauliflower is a low carb alternative for when you are craving mashed potatoes. This diabetes-friendly recipe is everything you could want out of a classic comfort food dish.
steps: Steam or boil the cauliflower florets until they are fork-tender, about 10–12 minutes.
Add the cook cauliflower to a large bowl.
In a small pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the garlic butter, salt, and pepper to the cauliflower.
Add Greek yogurt to the cauliflower.
Use a hand blender to blend the cauliflower until smooth and creamy.

title: Creamy Chicken Apple Salad
description: This salad is a low-carb, power-food dynamo. Easy to prepare and packed full of good nutrition—protein from chicken, fiber from the apple, and healthy fat from the walnuts—this is a quick diabetes-friendly recipe that's perfect for lunches and making ahead. Full of flavor and crunch—you won’t believe how easy it is!
steps: In a medium bowl, combine the chicken, celery, green onions, apple, and walnuts
In a small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice and pepper. Pour over the chicken mixture and gently stir to coat.
Serve salad over your choice of lettuce leaves, bread or crackers.

title: Sweet Potato Salad with Cilantro and Lime
description: This Tex-Mex style salad is hearty and filling and sure to rev up your taste buds. It’s diabetes-friendly and would work great as a side dish for your next taco Tuesday dinner!
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled and diced into bite-sized cubes)
1 (15 oz) can black beans (Reduced sodium, drained and rinsed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
Spread the seasoned sweet potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 30 minutes or until the sweet potatoes are tender and slightly caramelized, stirring halfway through.
While the sweet potatoes are roasting, prepare the dressing. Zest and juice the lime. In a small bowl, combine chopped fresh cilantro, lime zest, and lime juice.
Once the sweet potatoes are done, transfer them to a serving bowl.
Pour the cilantro and lime dressing over the roasted sweet potatoes.
Add finely chopped red onion, avocado, and black beans to the bowl.
Toss the salad gently to ensure even coating.

title: Cauliflower Tabbouleh
description: Tabbouleh is a traditional mediterranean salad made with flavorful herbs, fresh lemon, and couscous. This diabetes-friendly version uses cauliflower rice for lower carb, grain-free alternative.
ingredients: 1 head small head cauliflower (or 16-oz frozen cauliflower rice) (leaves and stem removed)
steps: Mince the parsley and mint leaves (or grind in a food processor) and add to a large bowl.
Grate the cauliflower using a box grater and stir together with the parsley and mint.
Add the diced tomato and stir it into the salad.
Drizzle the salad with the olive oil and lemon juice, and sprinkle with the salt (optional) and black pepper. Stir to coat.
Cover and let the tabbouleh marinate for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Easy Middle Eastern Green Beans
description:
This dish is inspired by a Lebanese dish called loubieh. It’s simply green beans and grape tomatoes cooked with a just-right amount of extra-virgin olive oil and seasoned with cinnamon and sea salt. It comes together quickly and can easily be made while the rest of your meal cooks. Pair it with a simple protein dish, like this Balsamic Glazed Salmon, for a quick and easy weeknight dinner.

Find this recipe and more in The Clean & Simple Diabetes Cookbook by Jackie Newgent, RDN, CDN
ingredients: 8 oz fresh green beans (stem ends trimmed)
steps: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the green beans and tomatoes, cover, and cook until the green beans are tender yet crisp and the tomatoes are fully softened, about 10 minutes. Toss with tongs a couple of times throughout the cooking.
Sprinkle the vegetables with the cinnamon and salt. Toss to combine, and then serve.

title: Whole-Wheat Spinach Parathas
description: Paratha is a type of flatbread that originated in the northern part of India, where it is still popular. It’s part of a traditional Indian breakfast, but can also be served alongside lunch or dinner.
ingredients: 2 cups plus 1 tbsp whole-wheat pastry flour (divided)
1 whole green chile (seeds discarded, finely minced)
steps: In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat 1 tsp oil over medium-high heat. Add the ajwain seeds, gingerroot, and chile. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring frequently.

Add the spinach and ¼ tsp salt. Cook for 3 minutes, or until the moisture released from the spinach is absorbed and the base becomes dry. Add the amchoor powder and cumin, stirring well. Remove from the heat. Set aside to cool.

To make the dough for the paratha: mix 2 cups flour and the remaining ¼ tsp salt in a shallow dish. Add the spinach mixture to the flour mixture. Add water, little by little, to form a smooth dough (similar to the consistency of a pizza dough). Knead the dough until smooth. Transfer to a glass bowl. Cover with a damp towel. Set aside for 30 minutes to an hour at room temperature.

After the standing time, knead the dough once again. Shape into 8 balls. Lightly dust your work surface with the remaining 1 Tbsp flour. Using a rolling pin, flatten each dough ball so it’s 6 inches in diameter.
Preheat a cast iron griddle or flat skillet over medium-high heat. Place one piece of dough in the skillet. Cook for about 1 minute, or until it begins to bubble.

Turn the paratha. Brush with ¼ tsp of the remaining oil. Continue cooking for about 3–4 minutes per side, turning as necessary, until the edges are brown on both sides. Using a flat spatula, press the middle of the paratha as it’s cooking so it cooks evenly.
Remove from the skillet. Repeat the cooking process with the remaining pieces of dough and remaining oil. Serve hot.

title: Caprese Kabobs
description: This easy appetizer is perfect for summer and uses garden fresh ingredients. These kabobs are packed with flavor and low in carbohydrates. They also look beautiful on a serving platter and are sure to impress guests!
ingredients: 18 whole fresh mozzarella balls (1/4 ounce each)
steps: Place 1 grape tomato, 1 basil leaf, and 1 mozzarella ball on each bamboo fork. Repeat this process for 18 kabobs. Place the kabobs on a serving platter.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil and balsamic vinegar. Right before serving, drizzle the dressing over the kabobs to coat evenly.

title: Blood Orange Salad (Insalata D’ Arrance Sangouse)
description: Sicily is known for its beautiful, lush orange groves, which produce some of the world’s most fragrant oranges. First introduced by the Arabs during their rule of the island, orange trees flourished in the ashes along the base of Mt. Etna. Look for the sweetest oranges possible for this recipe. If you can, use Sicilian blood oranges; their red color imparts festive flair to this sumptuous salad.
ingredients: 4 whole blood oranges (about 1 pound total, peeled and sliced into rounds)
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (preferably first cold-pressed and unfiltered)
steps: Place orange slices on a large platter and scatter green onions over the top.
In a small bowl, whisk orange juice and olive oil together, and season with salt, pepper, and crushed red chile flakes. Drizzle over the salad, and serve immediately.

title: Whipped Cottage Cheese Dip
description: Whipped Cottage Cheese Dip is a light and creamy alternative to traditional dips, providing a protein-packed option for snacking. Enjoy with your favorite veggies like broccoli, bell pepper, carrots, and more!
steps: In a blender or food processor, combine the low-fat cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, fresh lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and minced garlic. Blend the ingredients until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. This may take a few minutes, depending on the power of your blender or food processor.
Once the mixture is smooth, transfer it to a bowl. Stir in the chopped fresh chives and season the whipped cottage cheese dip with pepper. Mix well to ensure the flavors are evenly distributed.
Refrigerate the dip for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld and enhance the overall taste.

title: Beef Stroganoff
description: Whip up a hearty and flavorful dish that's sure to satisfy your cravings while helping to keep your blood glucose (blood sugar) levels in check. Learn step-by-step how to create a creamy, savory sauce paired with lean beef and wholesome ingredients, making this dish both delicious and mindful of your health. Whether you're cooking for yourself or your loved ones, this recipe is sure to become a staple in your kitchen.
ingredients: 1 lbs beef tenderloin (0" trim, sliced into 2-inch strips)
steps: Cook noodles according to package directions, omitting salt.
Add oil to a large sauté pan over high heat. Add meat and sauté for about 3 minutes. Remove meat from pan. Add mushrooms and onion and sauté for 5 minutes or until it begins to brown.
Add flour and cook for 1 minute. Add water gently to deglaze pan; cook for 2 minutes. Add Dijon mustard and beef broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add beef and any juices back to broth and simmer for 3 more minutes. Add sour cream and pepper; simmer for 30 seconds.
Serve over whole-grain egg noodles.

title: Healthy Snack Mix—Foodie Recipe
description: This snack mix is packed with nutrition and healthy fats from the many nuts and seeds. Plus the freeze-dried blueberries add a tangy, fruity flavor to the mix!
steps: Preheat an oven to 300 degrees F.
Coat a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray and set aside.
In a bowl, combine the brown sugar substitute, cayenne pepper, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, almonds and sesame seeds. Toss to coat.
Spread mixture onto the baking sheet and then spray again with a light coating of cooking spray.
Bake for 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes to ensure even browning.
Remove from oven and set aside to cool. When cool, toss the nut mixture in a bowl with the freeze-dried blueberries.

title: Savory Seaweed Edamame Yogurt Bowl
description: This savory yogurt bowl brings together creamy nonfat Greek yogurt, tender edamame, and the salty crunch of roasted seaweed for a high-protein, flavor-packed snack. It’s quick, refreshing, and delivers a sushi-inspired twist without any cooking.
steps: Add 1 cup nonfat Greek yogurt to a small bowl.
Stir in 1/2 cup shelled edamame until evenly distributed.
Crumble the pack of roasted seaweed over the top or fold it in for a softer texture.
Serve immediately so the seaweed stays crisp.

title: Black Bean Patties with Cilantro and Lime
description: Looking for a light summer burger? These black bean patties are delicious on a whole-grain bun, over a salad or simply on a plate with sliced onions.
ingredients: 1 can low sodium black beans (16-ounce can, do not drain)
1/4 cup, plus additional for dusting cornmeal (yellow or white)
1/4 cup cheddar cheese (reduced-fat, or use reduced-fat pepper Jack cheese)
1 spray, 0.25g nonstick cooking spray (for scoop or measuring cup)
steps: In a large nonstick pan heat olive oil and sauté onions, peppers, garlic, and spices. Sauté for 3 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.

Add black beans with liquid and sauté with vegetables for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Add breadcrumbs, cornmeal, lime juice, lime zest, and salt. Remove 1 cup of bean mixture and purée in a blender or food processor until a coarse purée is formed. Fold the purée back into the bean mixture. Add the cheddar cheese and cilantro, combine well. Mixture should resemble a coarse paste and be stiff enough to hold up in a scoop or spoon.

With an ice cream scoop or 1/3 cup measuring cup, form 3–4-ounce portions. (Spray the ice cream scoop or measuring cup lightly with cooking spray to make it easier to remove the mixture) Sprinkle a plate with cornmeal and place scooped black bean portions on plate. Lightly dust black bean mixture with cornmeal and press down gently, forming a patty.

Preheat oven to 375°F. Spray a large nonstick pan with vegetable oil. Brown patty cakes for 2 minutes on each side. If pan is ovenproof, transfer to oven and bake for 15 minutes or until heated through. Or transfer patty cakes to a cookie sheet pan and bake.

title: Cherry Oat Crisp
description: Cherry Oat Crisp is a delightful dessert that combines sweet and tart cherries with a crunchy oat topping. This healthier version is diabetes-friendly so everyone can enjoy.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a 9 x 9-inch baking dish with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the pitted cherries, lemon juice, zero-calorie maple syrup, and vanilla extract. Toss until the cherries are well coated.
Add the cherries to the prepared baking dish and spread in an even layer.
In a separate bowl, mix the oats, almond flour, chopped nuts, vegetable oil, and salt. Stir until the mixture is crumbly.
Sprinkle the oat mixture evenly over the top of the cherries.
Bake for about 30 minutes or until the cherry filling is bubbly, and the oat topping is golden brown.
Let it cool for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve warm.

title: Smoky Black Bean Dip
description: Dive into flavor paradise with our Smoky Black Bean Dip, a zesty sensation that transforms ordinary black beans into a smoky fiesta. Serve this dip with some fresh veggies for a healthy, low-carb snack or appetizer that’s perfect for people with and without diabetes.
serving_size: 1/4 cup dip + 1/2 cup sliced cucumber and bell pepper
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) black beans (No added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: Use a food processor to combine the drained and rinsed black beans, minced garlic, chopped fresh cilantro, lime juice, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Blend until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. You can gradually drizzle in 1 tablespoon of olive oil while blending to create your desired texture. Feel free to adjust the amount of oil according to your preference.
After blending, taste the dip and make any necessary adjustments to the seasonings. You can add more salt, pepper, or lime juice to suit your taste.
Transfer the black bean dip to a serving bowl and gently swirl in 2 tablespoons of plain Greek yogurt. This addition provides a creamy element and a touch of tanginess to the dip.
Serve with sliced cucumbers and bell peppers.

title: Grilled Portabellas with Tomato and Tuscan Herbs
description: These delicious mushrooms make a flavorful sandwich topped with a slice of fresh mozzarella or provolone and served on whole grain bread. Serve a mixed green salad on the side.
ingredients: 6 whole Portobello mushrooms (wiped clean and stem removed)
steps: Combine all of the marinade ingredients in a medium bowl and put into a large tightly sealed plastic bag. Marinate mushroom caps at least 15-30 minutes at room temperature for best results.

Preheat grill to medium high and place mushroom caps on grill grate. Cook under direct heat for 5 minutes per side until completely through to tender. Baste occasionally with additional marinade while cooking. You can pour any leftover marinade over mushrooms before serving.

title: Sauteed Fish Cakes
description: White fish, cod or tilapia are firm types of white fish that make excellent fish cakes. The Dijon mustard and lemon add a fresh, tangy flavor. Squeeze a little lemon juice on the top just before serving for more zip.
ingredients: 1 lbs white fish (patted dry, and cut into chunks)
steps: Add enough water to fill a large skillet 2/3 full. Over medium heat, bring the water to simmering. Add the fish and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through. Remove the fish chunks with a slotted spoon. Add the fish to a mixing bowl and let cool for 5 minutes.

Drain any excess liquid from the bowl. Add the yogurt, mustard, lemon juice, salt, lemon zest, and egg and mix well. Add ½ cup of the bread crumbs plus the scallions and hot sauce and mix well. Shape the fish mixture into 6 cakes. Coat each side of the cakes lightly with the remaining bread crumbs. Add the cakes to a plate and refrigerate, covered, for 30 minutes.

Remove the cakes from the refrigerator and let stand 5 minutes. In a large skillet, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the cakes to the skillet and sauté for about 5 minutes on each side, until golden brown.

title: Green Salad with Orange, Avocado, and Onion
description: Get creative with your oranges! Try navel, Valencia, Cara Cara, or blood oranges when you see them at your local market. They each have a slightly different delicious flavor but all of them are filled with vitamin C, fiber, and other good-for-you nutrients. Complete your plate: Add this salad to any meal that needs a vegetable boost. We've paired it with Southwest-Style Turkey Meatloaf and Mashed Red Potatoes.
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the lime juice, olive oil, red wine vinegar, sweetener, kosher salt, and black pepper.

Remove the peel and the white pith from around the oranges. Using a paring knife, cut in between the membranes to release the orange segments, and slice them into thirds. Place the orange pieces into a medium bowl.
Add the mixed greens, avocado cubes, and red onion to the bowl and drizzle with the lime juice mixture. Toss to combine. Sprinkle with the cilantro and serve.

title: Chile Lime Shrimp with Poblano Sauce
description: Chile Lime Shrimp with Poblano Sauce is a flavorful and zesty dish that combines the heat of chiles, the tanginess of lime, and the smokiness of poblano peppers.
ingredients: 1 lbs shrimp (peeled to just the tail and deveined)
steps: Line a sheet pan with parchment paper and preheat the broiler on high. Broil the poblano pepper until slightly blackened, for about 5 minutes, turning a couple of times. Place in a bowl and cover with plastic wrap to steam for 5 minutes.
Once it’s cool enough to touch, peel off the skin. Remove the stem and slice the pepper open to remove the seeds and roughly chop the pepper.
Toss the shrimp with ½ tablespoon olive oil, 1 garlic clove, peppers, and pepper.  Let it marinate for 15-30 minutes
While the shrimp is marinating, finish the sauce. Blend the poblano pepper, Greek yogurt, 2 grated garlic cloves, cumin, kosher salt, and pepper in a food processor until smooth.
Heat the remaining ½ tablespoon of olive oil in a skillet. Once the pan is hot, sear the shrimp for 2 minutes on each side until just cooked through.
Serve with the poblano sauce.

title: Budget-Friendly Herb Garlic Meatloaf
description:
This savory budget-friendly meat loaf is just as good as classic meatloaf. Our diabetes-friendly version is made with lean ground turkey and is seasoned with fresh herbs and garlic. For a complete meal, serve with over roasted sweet potatoes (they can roast alongside the meatloaf in the oven) and a nonstarchy vegetable side or simple green salad.

Powered by Homemade
steps: Pre heat oven to 375 degrees F. Coat a loaf pan with cooking spray. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, break up the piece of whole wheat bread into pea-sized pieces. Add egg and mix well.
Add turkey, garlic, oregano, basil, 1/4 cup ketchup, salt (optional) and ground black pepper. Mix well.
Press the turkey mixture into the loaf pan tightly. Put in oven to bake for 20 minutes.
While meatloaf is baking, whisk together remaining 1/4 cup of ketchup, balsamic vinegar and hot sauce (optional).

After the meatloaf has baked for 20 minutes, pour the ketchup and balsamic glaze over the meatloaf. Return to the oven to bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the internal temperature of the meatloaf is 165 degrees F.
Let the meatloaf rest for 10 minutes, then slice into 6 equal portions.

title: How to Make Harvest Salad
ingredients: 1 1/2 tbsp fresh mint (leaves, finely chopped plus more for garnish)
12 oz mixed greens (1 bag, mixed baby)
1/2 cup sugar snap peas (cut into 1/2-inch pieces)
1/8 tsp black pepper (freshly ground, to taste)
steps: To make the apple cider vinaigrette: Pour the apple cider vinegar into a bowl or a small jar with a lid. Add ¼ teaspoon of salt and shake or whisk to combine.
Add the Dijon mustard and olive oil and shake vigorously or whisk it well to combine.
Add the freshly chopped mint right before dressing the salad (otherwise it will turn brown).
To make the salad: In a large bowl, toss together the greens, radishes, sugar snap peas, half of the pepitas, and half of the pomegranate seeds.
Add a few tablespoons of the dressing and toss. You want the greens to be just barely coated with the dressing.
Taste and season with freshly ground black pepper as needed. Garnish with the remaining pepitas and pomegranate seeds before serving.

title: Pumpkin-Vanilla Pudding
description: Warm fall spices make this creamy pudding a festive holiday dessert!
steps: In a 3-quart saucepan, whisk together the sweetener and the corn starch.

In a small bowl, whisk together the milk and egg yolks. Over medium heat, slowly whisk the egg mixture into the sweetener mixture. Bring to boiling, continuing to whisk the mixture until it thickens, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the pumpkin, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, and nutmeg. Mix well and cook on low heat for 3 minutes. Add the vanilla bean seeds and cook 1 minute more.

Remove the saucepan from the stove. Place the pudding in a bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 1 hour before serving. To serve, spoon the pudding into individual dishes, top each dish with 1/2 Tbsp pecans, and dust with cinnamon. If desired, dollop with whipped topping.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Honey Mustard
description: Roasting vegetables brings the natural sugars to the surface making them less bitter and delicious. The honey mustard sauce give these brussels sprouts and added sweet tang.
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a flat baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss the trimmed sprouts with the olive oil, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Put the sprouts on the parchment-lined baking sheet in one single layer.
Roast the brussels sprouts for about 45 minutes or until crispy, shaking the sheet about every 15 minutes.
Mix together the mustard and honey in a small bowl. When the sprouts are done, add them to a serving bowl. Add in the honey mustard mixture, and toss well. Serve immediately.

title: Cinnamon Apple Oatmeal
description: Fresh apples make this oatmeal a perfect fall breakfast. A sprinkle of spices adds a depth of flavor to this diabetes-friendly Cinnamon Apple Oatmeal that the whole family will love.
steps: In a saucepan, bring water to a boil.
Stir in oats and reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5 minutes or until oats begin to thicken.
Add milk, diced apple, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until the oats are creamy, and the apples are tender (about 5 more minutes).
Remove from heat and let it sit for a minute to thicken.
Divide the oatmeal into two bowls. Serve warm.

title: Chicken Kale Salad with Fresh Ginger Dressing
description: This quick and easy salad is ready in a snap with just a few ingredients, perfect for a balanced and quick lunch or side dish.
serving_size: 2 cups salad + 3 ounces cooked chicken + 3 tbsp dressing
ingredients: 8 cup mixed greens (packed spinach with baby kale greens)
steps: Heat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. Coat the chicken with cooking spray, sprinkle with 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper, if desired. Cook 6 minutes on each side or until no longer pink in center. Let cool and thinly slice.
Place equal amounts of the greens and chicken on four dinner plates. Whisk together the salad dressing and ginger until well blended. Spoon equal amounts over all.

title: Oatmeal Congee
description: This version of what is a traditionally high-carb porridge is easy to make whole grain and healthy.
serving_size: ¾ cup porridge + 1 egg + 1 ½ tsp scallions and cilantro
steps: Add the oats, broth, and soy sauce to a sauce pan over high heat. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer until the oatmeal is tender, about 10 minutes.

Coat a small nonstick sauté pan with cooking spray. Add the mushrooms and sauté until tender and all liquid is evaporated, about 4 minutes. Add the lime juice and sauté until the liquid has evaporated. Stir the mushrooms into the oatmeal porridge.
Clean the sauté pan, then add cooking spray. Fry the eggs until the yolks are just set.
In a bowl, pour in ¾ cup oatmeal porridge, top with a fried egg, and 1 ½ Tsp. scallions and cilantro. Repeat for the remaining 3 bowls.

title: Sweet Potato Home Fries
description: Whether you are serving them for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, sweet potato home fries are always a family favorite. With tantalizing spices, this recipe will be one you want to make sure you save to make again and again.
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled and diced into small cubes)
steps: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the diced sweet potatoes to the skillet, spreading them out in a single layer.
Sauté the sweet potatoes for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are tender on the inside and crispy on the outside.
Sprinkle the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper over the sweet potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Cook for an additional 5 minutes, allowing the spices to meld with the sweet potatoes.
Remove the skillet from the heat.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

title: Curried Tomato Coconut Lentils over Cauliflower Rice
description: This perfectly spiced Curried Tomato Coconut Lentils is a vegetarian dish that is also a nutritious and diabetes friendly option.
ingredients: 1 cup lentils (green or brown, dry, rinsed)
1 (14 oz) can canned diced tomatoes (low sodium)
½ (14 oz) can lite coconut milk
steps: In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot. Sauté for an additional 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the curry powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper. Cook the spices with the onion mixture for 1–2 minutes.
Add the rinsed lentils, diced tomatoes, and coconut milk to the pot. Stir well to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot and let it simmer for 20–25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
Serve over the steamed cauliflower rice and garnish with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro, if desired.

title: Vegetarian Breakfast Burrito Bowl
description: This colorful and veggie-filled breakfast burrito bowl offers a twist on the classic by using whole grain quinoa instead of white rice as the base. This recipe can be used for breakfast, lunch, or dinner because it is an excellent source of fiber, a good source of protein, and includes non-starchy vegetables.
ingredients: 1 cup quinoa (cooked without salt or fat)
1 med avocado (diced, optional: use half for reduced fat)
steps: Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add spinach and sauté until wilted (about 2 minutes).
Whisk eggs with cumin and paprika, then pour into the skillet with spinach. Scramble until cooked through.
Assemble the bowl. Divide cooked quinoa, black beans, tomatoes, avocado, and scrambled eggs among 4 bowls.
Drizzle with lime juice.

title: Pumpkin-Banana Muffins
description:
Start your morning with a sweet, diabetes friendly treat with these pumpkin-banana muffins. Lower in carbs than store-bought muffins, pair this with a cup of coffee for the perfect start to your day.

Add a Microwave Egg and Veggie Jar or Spinach and Egg Bites to help round out your breakfast with some veggies and protein!
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F and line a muffin tin with liners.
Mix flour, sugar, baking soda, salt, pumpkin pie spice in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, mix together the eggs, pumpkin puree, oil, banana, and vanilla.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir to combine. Gently fold in the walnuts.
Scoop the batter into muffin tins and bake for 18-20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.

title: Southwest-Style Turkey Meatloaf
description: A nice way to add whole grains into protein dishes—such as meatloaf, hamburgers, and meatballs—is to use quick-cooking oats instead of regular bread crumbs. The fiber in the oats has been shown to help lower cholesterol. Complete your Plate: For a classic "meat-and-potatoes" meal, pair with Mashed Red Potatoes. Add a Green Salad with Orange and Avocado for a balanced meal.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Coat a 9 × 5-inch loaf pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Add all of the remaining ingredients to a large bowl. Gently mix the ingredients until well combined.

Spoon the mixture into the prepared loaf pan, using the back of the spoon or a spatula to even out the top. Place the loaf pan in the oven and bake until a thermometer inserted into the center of the meatloaf reads 165°F, 1 hour.

title: Maple Apples
description: Sautéing apples caramelizes their natural sugars creating a rich, sweet flavor. These apples are tossed in a low sugar syrup made from apple cider and sugar-free maple syrup for a delicious, diabetes-friendly dessert. Or, serve over plain Greek yogurt for a sweet but filling breakfast.
ingredients: 2 med Granny Smith or other tart apple (unpeeled and sliced into 1/2-inch wedges)
steps: Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice.

In a large skillet, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the apples and sauté for 3 minutes. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 6 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove the apples from the pan and set aside.

In the same skillet add all the remaining ingredients except the almonds. Bring to a boil and cook over medium-high heat until syrupy, scraping up any bits of apple remaining in the pan. Add back the apples and sprinkle with the sliced almonds.
